corrected_content.problem:
The matrix $P$ is given below. Let ${p}_{1}$, ${p}_{2}$,  ${p}_{3}$ and ${p}_{4}$ be the respective columns of $P.$
Determine if $B=\left\{{p}_{1},{p}_{2}\right\}$ is a basis of $\text{Col}(P).$ 
If that is the case, find ${x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{2}$, where ${p}_{4}={x}_{1}{p}_{1}+{x}_{2}{p}_{2}.$ 

$$
P=\begin{bmatrix}1 & 0 & -3 & 2 \\ 2 & 3 & -3 & 1 \\ -5 & -3 & 13 & -7\end{bmatrix}
$$
corrected_content.worked_solution:
First, we reduce the matrix $P$ to reduced row echelon form (RREF):

$$
\begin{aligned}P & =\begin{bmatrix}1 & 0 & -3 & 2 \\ 2 & 3 & -3 & 1 \\ -5 & -3 & 13 & -7\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & 0 & -3 & 2 \\ 0 & 3 & 3 & -3 \\ -5 & -3 & 13 & -7\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+5{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & 0 & -3 & 2 \\ 0 & 3 & 3 & -3 \\ 0 & -3 & -2 & 3\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{2} & :=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & 0 & -3 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & -3 & -2 & 3\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+3{R}_{2} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & 0 & -3 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

From the matrix above, we see that the pivot columns are the $1$st, $2$nd, and $3$rd columns. So, a basis of $\text{Col}(P)$ is $\{{p}_{1},{p}_{2},{p}_{3}\}.$ 

Therefore, we conclude that $B=\{{p}_{1},{p}_{2}\}$ is not a basis of $\text{Col}(P).$
